programme_detail_official.description: The Australia Awards Fellowships program is a competitive grants program administered by DFAT that funds eligible Australian organisations to host mid-career and senior officials from partner-country organisations for short-term development activities in Australia. Fellowships range from 2 to 52 weeks and can combine short-term study or training, research, professional attachments and networking, and they do not lead to academic qualifications. DFAT funding of up to AUD 34,500 per Fellow is offered on a competitive basis, and host organisations must contribute in kind or financially. Applications are submitted by Australian organisations rather than by individuals.
programme_detail_official.region: ODA-eligible developing countries, including the Pacific, South and Southeast Asia, South Asia and the Middle East, Africa and the Caribbean
programme_detail_official.coverage: DFAT funding up to AUD 34,500 per Fellow plus a mandatory host-organisation in-kind or financial co-contribution; itemised budget categories are published in the Round guidelines and fact sheet, which could not be retrieved in this pass

Confirm the proposed Fellowship is 2 to 52 weeks, includes at least two weeks in Australia, and spends less time in partner countries than in Australia

Download the guidelines, budget table and industry briefing for the current Round and follow the published application compliance criteria
Confirm the Round is open on the DFAT page before submitting, because rounds close on fixed published dates
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an individual instead of through a registered Australian organisation with a current ABN
The Overseas Counterpart Organisation being an international branch of the applicant or under the same parent organisation
Proposing a Fellowship outside the 2-52 week window or with more time in partner countries than in Australia
Nominating a Fellow who holds, or is applying for, Australian citizenship or permanent residency
Nominating a Fellow who cannot travel without family members
Failing to demonstrate genuine links with the eligible Overseas Counterpart Organisation
Missing the published round closing date, after which DFAT will not accept applications
estimated_uncovered_costs: The portion of Fellowship costs not met by the DFAT contribution of up to AUD 34,500 per Fellow, which the host organisation must fund as its co-contribution

programme_detail_official.description: The Australia Awards Mekong-Australia Partnership scholarships are a DFAT-funded stream of the Australia Awards Scholarships, announced at the ASEAN-Australia Special Summit in March 2024 as part of a further five-year commitment to the Mekong subregion. From 2026 MAP offers postgraduate scholarships at Master's level, by coursework or by research, for citizens of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar, provided the study or research sits within one of the MAP thematic areas. MAP-funded scholarship benefits are the same as the wider Australia Awards Scholarship benefits, with exclusive access to the Mekong-Leaders Network on-award enrichment program.
programme_detail_official.region: Mekong subregion (Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar), delivered at Australian institutions
programme_detail_official.coverage: Full tuition fees, return air travel, establishment allowance, fortnightly Contribution to Living Expenses, Introductory Academic Program, Overseas Student Health Cover, possible pre-course English and possible supplementary academic support or fieldwork airfare

programme_detail_official.description: The Research Training Program is an Australian Government block-grant programme that funds eligible higher education providers to support domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorate and research masters degrees. Students may be offered an RTP tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances for the ancillary costs of higher degree by research. Applications are made directly to individual higher education providers, each of which runs its own selection process, so there is no single application portal or closing date. The Commonwealth indexes the base and maximum stipend rates annually and publishes them by 1 October each year.

programme_detail_official.region: Australia, at eligible higher education providers
programme_detail_official.coverage: Provider-level packages combining a possible tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs and HDR ancillary allowances; indexed full-time stipend rates are AUD 34,315 base and AUD 53,608 maximum for 2026, and AUD 35,550 base and AUD 55,537 maximum for 2027

application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist eligible higher education providers that offer an RTP in your chosen discipline and confirm their 2027 HDR intake dates
Apply directly to each provider, because the Department of Education does not accept RTP applications
Prepare a research proposal or confirm your research topic, as the award is restricted to research doctorate and research masters degrees
Check whether the provider's package includes a tuition offset, a stipend, or both, and ask for the exact stipend rate it will use
Note that stipend rates differ by study load: part-time research doctorate support runs 6 to 8 years versus 3 to 4 years full-time
Register or update your ORCID profile and be ready to add the RTP DOI to it and to any resulting publications
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an application to the Department of Education, which does not accept RTP applications
Missuing the individual provider's HDR closing date, which is often much earlier than the academic calendar suggests
Applying to a coursework master's rather than a research master's or research doctorate
Assuming the indexed maximum stipend rate applies automatically, since providers set the rate within the published base and maximum
Expecting travel funding, which is not listed among the RTP components
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition shortfall if the provider's RTP package does not include a fees offset
Living costs beyond the provider's stipend rate, which is set somewhere between the published base and maximum

Travel costs, which are not among the published RTP components

programme_detail_official.description: The Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship is offered by the University of Melbourne to international students enrolling in a bachelor's degree who are citizens of countries where international educational opportunities are limited by financial disadvantage, defined on the official page as countries with a GDP per capita of US$10,000 or less. The award is a tuition fee remission rather than a full scholarship: 25 per cent for awards made before 2027 and 20 per cent from 2027, applied for the duration of the course. No separate application is needed, because consideration is automatic for anyone who applies for a course, and selection ranks the highest-scoring applicants on final secondary school or foundation results.
